key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over days to weeks, often triggered by stress, weather, or irritants. LOCATION: FLEXURAL areas (elbows, knees, neck), face, hands, or generalized. DURATION: Chronic condition with acute flares lasting days to weeks. CHARACTER: ERYTHEMATOUS (red), PRURITIC (itchy), DRY, SCALY skin. AGGRAVATING: SCRATCHING, heat, stress, certain fabrics, soaps. RELIEVING: MOISTURIZERS, topical steroids, antihistamines, avoiding triggers. TIMING: Chronic with acute flares, worse at night. SEVERITY: 4-8/10 itching, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SEVERE ITCHING (pruritus), dry skin, scaling, may have lichenification (thickened skin), may have secondary infection from scratching. KEY POSITIVES: Erythema, pruritus, scaling, lichenification, flexural distribution. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no systemic symptoms, no vesicles or bullae (unless secondary infection).

red_flags: Rash with fever and systemic symptoms - possible secondary infection, needs urgent evaluation
Rash with pus or increasing pain - secondary bacterial infection, needs urgent evaluation
Rash involving >30% of body surface - severe flare, needs urgent evaluation
Rash with signs of secondary infection - fever, pus, increasing pain - needs urgent evaluation
Rash with difficulty sleeping due to severe itching - severe flare, needs urgent evaluation
